Switching from a calendar time

Source: vignettes/calendar-switching.Rmd
calendar-switching.Rmd
library(DesignComplexSurvival)

Switching to the experimental treatment is sometimes allowed only from a calendar time, for example after an interim analysis has shown a benefit. With switch_start in ms_scenario(), nobody switches before that calendar time (time since the start of accrual). A patient enrolled at time e can switch from the follow-up time max(switch_start - e, 0) on: a progression before that time does not lead to a switch at progression, and a patient who progressed before it can switch with switch_rate from that time on.

Scenario

The models are those of vignette("switching"): in the control group 30 percent of the patients switch at progression and the others may switch later with a hazard of 0.04 per month; the death hazard after progression is 0.06 without switch and 0.035 after a switch. The post-progression intensities are constant, so that the reset and forward clocks give the same model; the forward clock is used here because its computations with switch_start are faster.

ctl <- ms_model(time = c(0, 4), prog = c(0.10, 0.08), death = 0.01,
                switch_prob = 0.3, death_prog = 0.06, switch_rate = 0.04,
                death_switch = 0.035, dropout = 0.003, clock = "forward")
trt <- ms_model(time = c(0, 4), prog = c(0.06, 0.05), death = 0.008,
                death_prog = 0.055, dropout = 0.003, clock = "forward")
acc <- ms_accrual(rate = 25)
looks <- ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.6, 1))

Power by the start of switching

The design enrolls 500 patients and analyses OS at 60 percent of the final 300 deaths and at 300 deaths. The power and the type I error for switching from randomization (switch_start = 0) and from months 6 to 24:

starts <- c(0, 6, 12, 18, 24)
res <- lapply(starts, function(s)
  ms_power(ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = acc, switch_start = s), n = 500,
           looks = looks, test = ms_test(), events = 300))
tab <- data.frame(switch_start = starts,
                  power = sapply(res, function(x) x$power),
                  type1 = sapply(res, function(x) x$type1[["nonbinding"]]),
                  interim = sapply(res, function(x) x$looks$time[1]),
                  final = sapply(res, function(x) x$study_duration))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 4, 5, 1, 1))
switch_start power type1 interim final
0 0.2206 0.02500 28.8 43.9
6 0.2507 0.02500 28.7 43.8
12 0.3446 0.02502 28.5 43.5
18 0.5033 0.02504 28.0 42.9
24 0.6736 0.02504 27.7 42.2 
plot(tab$switch_start, tab$power, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Calendar month from which switching is possible", ylab = "Power")

When switching starts later, fewer control patients have switched by the time of the analyses. The power is 0.221 with switching from randomization and 0.674 with switching from month 24, and the interim analysis takes place at month 28.8 and month 27.7, respectively.

Type I error

The distribution of OS now depends on the entry time. Under the null hypothesis (ms_null(), the control model with its switching in both groups) the switching still changes the death hazard, so that the score no longer has independent increments. The correlation between the looks is computed from the per-patient influence functions, integrated over the entry time (see ?lr_cov). The efficacy bounds still come from the event fractions, so that the type I error computed with the exact correlation can differ from 0.025: it ranges from 0.025 to 0.02504 in the table above.

Scope

The computations with switch_start cover the OS statistic alone with mean = "direct". PFS is not affected by the switching. Two endpoints tested together, an OS test at looks driven by PFS events, switching before progression and the Schoenfeld approximation of the mean give an error:

scn12 <- ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = acc, switch_start = 12)
err <- function(expr) tryCatch({
  expr
  "no error"
}, error = conditionMessage)
err(ms_power(scn12, n = 500, looks = looks, test = ms_test(mean = "schoenfeld"),
             events = 300))
#> [1] "Switching from a calendar time ('switch_start') needs mean = \"direct\" for OS."
err(ms_power(scn12, n = 500, looks = ms_looks("pfs", fraction = c(0.6, 1)),
             test = ms_test(), events = 300))
#> [1] "With switching from a calendar time ('switch_start'), the looks of an OS test cannot be driven by PFS events."

ms_size() solves for the number of events, the sample size, the accrual duration or the follow-up with switch_start in the same way as without it.
